newsitem.title: UK: Gold easier, base metals firmer as pre-Christmas mood prevails.
newsitem.headline: Gold easier, base metals firmer as pre-Christmas mood prevails.

text.p: Gold was slightly easier on Wednesday and base metal prices were in comfortable ranges in subdued activity ahead of next week's Christmas holidays.

"Things are getting very much into a pre-Christmas vein. It is going to take a big move in the dollar or something to get anything moving," one dealer said. Platinum's price, which helped the precious metals complex hold higher overnight levels, held just below its early high at $370.50/$371.50, still up $2.65 on the day after a burst of short covering on the Tokyo futures December contract.
"It was the last dealing day for December contract on Tocom and people were expecting a lot of selling. When that did not happen, they were caught a bit on the hop," a dealer said.
Gold bullion was fixed at $368.85/$369.35 against Tuesday's close of $368.70/$369.20.

Dealers said the selling by producers which had depressed the market recently had dried up ahead of next week's holiday, but the decision by Washington on Tuesday night not to raise U.S. interest rates had not been a significant factor.
Base metal prices on the London Metal Exchange (LME) were generally firmer with sentiment improving in aluminium, and copper hovering around $2,100 in subdued trade to finish at day's highs.

"Sentiment towards aluminium is improving nicely with IPAI (International Primary Aluminium Institute) producer stocks falling by 433,000 tonnes, or 20 percent, since January whilst over the same period LME stocks have risen by just 297,000 tonnes," analyst Nick Moore of Flemings Global Mining Group said in a commentary.
In the soft commodity markets, coffee and cocoa ended mostly firm while sugar were mixed.
Cocoa bounced from nine-month lows on short covering triggered by a strong New York performance.
